title: Phil Rudd - Wikipedia
notes: Phillip Hugh Norman Rudd, born Phillip Hugh Norman Witschke Rudzevecuis, 19 May 1954, Melbourne. AC/DC's drummer 1975-1983, 1994-2015 and from 2018; Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, 2003. Buster Brown with Angry Anderson (Something to Say, 1974), then the Coloured Balls with Lobby Loyde. Told of AC/DC's auditions by Trevor Young; hired on the spot. Parted from the band in 1983 after his parts for Flick of the Switch were done, partly through a conflict with Malcolm Young; B.J. Wilson's parts were not used; Simon Wright replaced him. Brian Johnson: 'You couldn't find a more solid person or drummer than Phil Rudd.' In New Zealand, flying helicopters, racing cars, farming; played 'when I wanted to rather than when I had to'. Rejoined in 1994 after Big Gun; the band 'maintained that a certain groove had been missing from AC/DC's music since Rudd's departure'. Ballbreaker, Stiff Upper Lip, Black Ice, Rock or Bust, Power Up. Replaced by Chris Slade for the 2015-2016 tour; by Matt Laug for the 2024 Power Up tour. Head Job (2014), a solo album.

title: AC/DC - Wikipedia
notes: Peter Clack played on one track of High Voltage (1975), Tony Currenti on the rest; Clack fired in January 1975; Ron Carpenter and Russell Coleman briefly, then Phil Rudd from Buster Brown that month. T.N.T. recorded with Evans and Rudd except two tracks, Currenti and George Young. David Marchese (Vulture): the foundation of the band's sound was the drummer, Rudd, Wright or Slade, 'striking the kick drum on the first and third beat of every measure and the snare drum on the second and fourth', Cliff Williams down-picking eighths on the bass, Malcolm's rhythm guitar 'propulsive' with 'little chuks, stutters, and silences'. A 1996 photograph: shoulder-length hair, a dark T-shirt, a cigarette, a tattoo on the upper arm.

title: Phil Rudd interview, Cyber Drum, 15 August 2000 (Molson Centre, Montreal), by Steven Scott Fyfe
notes: Reposted on a fan blog; the cyberdrum.com original was not reached. The rhythm section is Cliff, Malcolm and him: 'we all lock together to get the groove'; 'if one person decides to go by himself, this doesn't mean anything'; 'We all listen to each other to lock and be tight.' Has never used a click: 'you can't rock to a click, it just doesn't happen'; each riff has its own speed and feel. Tuning: 'If you can't feel it you can't tune it.' Sonor drums; one rack tom, two large floor toms, a 24-inch bass drum, a 5 3/4-inch snare. An early 'speed period' of fast fills and rudiments, then feel: play the whole song, not 'pretentious'. First inspiration: the Small Faces' Tin Soldier, its breakdown into the guitar. Stiff Upper Lip 'in a lot of ways is my favorite album'.

title: Phil Rudd: Bukowski with a Backbeat (Joe Daly)
notes: Rudd: 'It's a process of suspension and release ... It's like having sex, you have to find the right groove.' 'Being a drummer in AC/DC you are the boss of the engine room, and you have to assure that all the parts are kept together.' On a replacement: 'He didn't have the groove.' Daly: 'his gift was subtraction'.

title: Phil Rudd: The Very Definition of Rock Drumming (Modern Drummer, 27 May 2011)
notes: 'No-nonsense, rock-solid, play-for-the-song drumming'; 'dogged consistency and unshakeable backbeat' on It's a Long Way to the Top, T.N.T. and Dirty Deeds; his 'unselfish style and humongous groove' admired by generations of drummers; Kenny Aronoff and Eric Singer call his feel 'the heart and soul of AC/DC'. Modern Drummer, May 2010: 'Reasons to Love Phil Rudd', 'the rock drummer'.

title: 6 Mistakes Drummers Make When Covering AC/DC (Dave Atkinson, Drumeo)
notes: Updated 21 November 2023. 'Phil isn't just playing consistent 8th notes on the hi-hat in every song'; listen to how loose or tight the hats are, 'many positions between 100% open and 100% closed'. 'A loud and consistent backbeat (let someone else worry about ghost notes) and a beefy snare crack'; rimshots in the chorus; 'shots (bass, snare, crash) on both the downbeat and backbeat, as well as pushes on the and of 4'.

title: AC/DC "Back In Black" auf dem Schlagzeug lernen (Bonedo, 12 January 2015)
notes: Straight eighths on the hats, the kick on 1 and 3, the snare on 2 and 4; the fourth bar's fill in groups of three from 2, the snare and the kick with the hat. Probably a Sonor Phonic kit, a Sonor Phonic D505 snare, Paiste 2002 cymbals (14-inch medium hats). Tony Platt's recording: two U87 overheads, a KM86 on the snare and an SM57 under it, SM7s on the toms, a U47 on the kick; gated, pitched down a little through an Eventide H910, a short delay on the snare, not compressed.

title: Inside Track: AC/DC 'Black Ice' (Paul Tingen, Sound On Sound, January 2009)
notes: Mike Fraser: a small drum booth built inside the live room of the Warehouse's Studio 2, 'just big enough for Phil to swing his stick in'; 'They don't like things roomy or bombastic, they're more a thumping, let's-get-your-foot-stomping kind of band'; backing tracks in 'three or four takes', to analogue tape. Two SM57s on the snare, a KM84 on the hats, U87s or U47s overhead.

title: AC/DC, Highway to Hell (the 1979 promotional film, official video)
notes: The band miming the song on a stage, 1979; the remastered upload 0m1j-mr7mpQ, Rudd at the kit at 0:09-0:17 and 2:12-2:16. Slim, twenty-five, mid-brown hair to the shoulders with a fringe, a moustache, a white T-shirt, a tattoo on the upper arm; a dark kit with chrome hardware, white heads, brass cymbals.

title: T.N.T. (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 1 December 1975 in Australia and New Zealand, Albert Productions; Albert Studios, Sydney, produced by Vanda and Young. Rudd: drums and percussion on tracks 1-7 (It's a Long Way to the Top, Rock 'n' Roll Singer, The Jack, Live Wire, T.N.T., Rocker, Can I Sit Next to You Girl); Tony Currenti on 8-9 (High Voltage, School Days). It's a Long Way to the Top edited down from a jam; George Young's idea for the bagpipes.

title: Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap - Wikipedia
notes: Released 20 September 1976. Recorded at Albert Studios with Vanda and Young from December 1975. Phil Rudd: drums.

title: Let There Be Rock - Wikipedia
notes: Released 21 March 1977 in Australasia, internationally 25 July 1977. Albert Studios, Sydney; Vanda and Young. Phil Rudd: drums, percussion.

title: Highway to Hell - Wikipedia
notes: Released 27 July 1979. Recorded 24 March to 14 April 1979 at the Roundhouse, London, produced by Mutt Lange (after sessions with Eddie Kramer); mixed by Tony Platt. Phil Rudd: drums.

title: Back in Black - Wikipedia
notes: Released 25 July 1980; recorded April to May 1980 at Compass Point, Nassau, with Mutt Lange, Brian Johnson's first album after Bon Scott's death. Hells Bells, Back in Black, You Shook Me All Night Long. Phil Rudd: drums. Robert Christgau on You Shook Me All Night Long: 'a drum-hooked fucksong' (the song's article).

title: Black Ice (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 17 October 2008. Recorded 3 March to 25 April 2008 at the Warehouse, Vancouver, with Brendan O'Brien, engineered by Mike Fraser. O'Brien tried to recapture the sound of Highway to Hell and Dirty Deeds. Rock 'n' Roll Train the lead single, 'centred around guitar riffs and elemental drum beats'. Phil Rudd: drums.
